question: Make the 'recent ruling' flag time-correct. For the 29,082 top-50 FY2023-24 Schedule I lines whose EO BMF ruling month is on or after (grant-year start - 24 months), take the ruling month from archived BMF extracts of 2023-2025 (IRS SOI eo1-eo4 as first published in those years, or a dated public mirror) instead of the 2026-11 snapshot. Split true new organisations from reinstatements and re-determinations, and re-run scripts/mission_exception_load.py.
conclusion_affected: Size of the 'new grantee' review cohort, which is the largest single driver of the core exception proxy (4.8% of lines, 5.9% of dollars)
rationale: The BMF RULING field is a 2026-11 snapshot. 4,090 flagged lines ($588.8m) carry a ruling month after the grant year ended, which fits reinstatement or re-determination better than a new charity. The recent-ruling share may therefore overstate first-time grantees

question: Turn Schedule I recipient lines into a per-grant count for at least four top-50 sponsors that publish annual grant counts (e.g. NPT's 159,543 grants in FY2025), and estimate the exception share by number of grants rather than by recipient line. Use each sponsor's own annual report or impact report for FY2023-2025, and include the sub-$5,000 grants that Schedule I does not itemise.
conclusion_affected: Whether the core exception share by grant count is closer to 7% (recipient lines) or to the 0.3-1% floor previously inferred for nationals
rationale: Schedule I lists each recipient once per year and only when above $5,000. Many small retail grants to listed public charities are therefore missing from the denominator, so the line-count share overstates the per-grant share. No public per-grant denominator has yet been matched to Schedule I in the repo

question: Replace the 19-name fiscal-sponsor list with a fuller, EIN-keyed list of US fiscal sponsors from a public directory (e.g. the Fiscal Sponsor Directory or the National Network of Fiscal Sponsors member list, robots permitting). Re-score the top-50 Schedule I lines, and report how far the fiscal-sponsor share (1.30% of dollars, 0.12% of lines) moves.
conclusion_affected: Fiscal-sponsor component of the exception proxy; the 10.7x dollar-to-count ratio
rationale: The current list is the Q-B15 list of 19 large hosts matched by name. Generic markers ('fiscal sponsor', 'a project of') add only $55k, so smaller hosts are almost certainly missed

question: Check the expenditure-responsibility (ER) cases named by the proxy against the grantors' own disclosures: Founders Pledge Inc (BMF foundation code 04 but Pub 78 PC; $53.9m from top-50 sponsors), Huntington Foundation (PF; $43.6m from Columbus Foundation) and the community foundations with the largest PF/ER shares (Community Foundation of New Jersey 12.6%, Columbus Foundation 8.7%). Use Schedule I Part I narratives, Schedule O and the recipients' Forms 990-PF for FY2023-2024.
conclusion_affected: ER component of the proxy; whether CF PF/ER dollars are DAF grants or discretionary grants
rationale: Pub 78 and the BMF disagree on Founders Pledge's foundation status. Community foundations' Schedule I also mixes DAF and non-DAF grants, so CF PF/ER shares are upper bounds

question: Explain the two largest single-line drivers of sponsor-level exception dollars: Greater Horizons FY2024's Schedule I line with no recipient name and no EIN ($212.2m, half of its $424.4m FY2024 Schedule I), and SVCF FY2023's $1.309bn line to Further Future Foundation (EIN 92-1117448, BMF ruling 2023-03). Use the filers' Schedule I Part I and Schedule O text and the recipient's own Form 990 for 2023-2024.
conclusion_affected: Greater Horizons' 59.8% and SVCF's 45.8% dollar exception shares; the community-foundation pooled dollar-vs-count gap (+11.4 pp)
rationale: Without these two lines the community-foundation and Greater Horizons dollar shares fall sharply. The all-sponsor core dollar share is 11.2% with SVCF and 9.8% without it and without university/hospital sponsors

question: Re-run the exception-load proxy on FY2025 returns (tax periods ending in 2025) once the GivingTuesday mirror holds the top-50 Schedule I/F, and report the year-on-year change by sponsor type. Reuse scripts/mission_exception_load.py with a FY2025 line cache and the Schedule F sponsor-year rows rebuilt for FY2025.
conclusion_affected: Stability of the 7.4%/11.2% core proxy, and comparability with the four-national FY6/2025 figure (2.5-3%)
rationale: The four-national comparison mixes FY6/2025 (earlier work) with FY2023-24 (this proxy). NPT's foreign share is 7.4% in FY2023-24 against 4.84% in FY6/2025, so the year matters
